source.title: Longest Subarray With Maximum Bitwise AND

teaching.hint: Can adding another positive number to a bitwise AND ever raise the result above a single array element?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The AND of a subarray cannot exceed any of its elements. Its maximum over all nonempty subarrays is therefore the array's largest element, achieved by a singleton; a longer subarray preserves that value only if every element equals it.
solution_outline.approach: Find the maximum array value, then scan for the longest contiguous run equal to that value.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The current run length is the number of consecutive maximum-valued elements ending at the current position, and the best length is the greatest such run encountered.
solution_outline.correctness: Any subarray AND is at most each included value and thus at most the global maximum; a singleton at that maximum attains it. If a subarray also attains it, each constituent must be at least the global maximum and therefore equal to it. Conversely, a run of equal maximum values has that same AND, so its longest run length is exactly the answer.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space for n positive integers.
solution_outline.pitfall: Counting all occurrences of the maximum ignores the requirement that the qualifying subarray be contiguous.

common_wrong_turns: Combine disjoint occurrences of the maximum
Search every subarray for its AND
Assume a longer subarray can have AND above its elements
source_fidelity_notes: The source example was kept in compact form; nonempty contiguity, two-stage maximum-and-longest objective, positivity, and bounds were retained.
